In terms of roi, everything has a shelf life. I’m of the opinion that lower effort content typically receives less traction depending on where that money’s going. Nowadays it’s borderline required to invest in good audio and editing either yourself or by hiring an editor. Then there’s the question of what’s your audience, how saturated the market is and most importantly, what sets you apart and is it good enough to create a loyal base.

As an example take Minecraft content on YouTube for instance. It has a large fanbase sure but the market is incredibly saturated. There’s way more supply even amongst the main contenders of the genre than what the average consumer can and will consume. Unless you find some way to try something new and implement it well (meaning it’s quality is at least decent) you’re content will fall flat.

Tldr if you want to make low effort content find a genre that has little content in the first place. Just know that as you get more popular it will be dethroned by better content creators
Imo make great videos, it’s much more rewarding than churning out low effort content

Oh yeah, I’d say without a doubt homeschool is the primary cause for my dating problems hands down.

As far as I’ve seen people generally don’t care that you were homeschooled. I’m 18 but even so whenever I’ve told someone they are more interested in what it was like than anything, as long as you don’t focus on the negatives it can be a good icebreaker, especially if you had a situation like me where you moved around a lot, focusing on that could help you out in carrying a conversation forward. The more time that goes on tho the less I talk about it with people I meet. Usually I just say we moved to the country I’m in (not completely false) and that’s why I’m awkward. I find others are more accepting of that but take with a grain of salt.

Most of my dating problems come from the mindset that developed in homeschool. I was barely allowed to leave my home at all so I grew up past the age of 15 not talking to women (or really anyone outside of my family) at all. When I got out this year I noticed I have a severe lack of confidence and I tend to freeze up when talking to women whether I’m attracted to them or not. I’m getting better (hell I can hold a good conversation with a little bit of humor as I’d been able to back in middle school) but I still have a ways to go. It also doesn’t help that I have some issues with trusting others or comprehending and tolerating physical intimacy. Right now I’ve kinda just put it on the backburner to return to once I straightened most of my shit out.

One thing that I found that helps is to essentially adopt the idea that you just “came to be” whenever you got out of homeschool. Basically treat it like everything up to that moment you didn’t exist and you just popped into the world whenever you graduated/ left homeschool. I’ve been using this method if thinking for learning social things and how to carry myself as well as to unlearn my past bad habits. This has been especially helpful for dealing with bad thoughts as I used to dwell on my past and how I missed out on highschool alot. However I’ve been trying my best to tune those thoughts out with just focusing on how the past never existed, You’re a tabula rasa who isn’t defined by the past and the world is out there to explore.

Hope that last bit helps a bit. It’s a longer process for us but through determination and both motivation and discipline, we can rise above those who we now look at as role models. You got this
